source.title: Descriptor-Injected Cross-Modal Learning: A Systematic Exploration of Audio-MIDI Alignment via Spectral and Melodic Features

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures cross-modal representational alignment between audio and MIDI encoders, a new modality setting for the claim. It does not test scaling with model size.
record.gate_note: The CKA and RSA measurements, and the reported matched-pair cosine comparison, directly bear on cross-modal alignment. Retrieval scores are recorded separately as performance findings; they do not themselves measure alignment. Screening results, ablations, robustness tests, and probes are omitted where they do not measure alignment or its relation to capability.
record.test_reason: This study does not test any version. The audio and MIDI encoders are trained jointly with a VICReg loss whose invariance term directly minimises the distance between matched audio–MIDI embeddings. Cross-modal alignment is therefore the training target, not something that arises in independently trained models. The CKA, RSA and cosine numbers measure how strongly descriptor injection increases this deliberately trained alignment within one dual-encoder system. No independently trained models, scale or capability sweep, or vision–language pair is involved. The paper uses 'representational convergence' to mean that its two encoders grow more similar, not in the Platonic or convergent-learning sense, and it never cites either original.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that descriptors (especially A4) improve retrieval and roughly double cross-encoder CKA, which they read as the encoders converging on a 'shared language'. They also note that the highest CKA (d4-a4r) does not give the best retrieval. They hypothesise that excessive alignment homogenises representations and costs discriminative detail. All alignment diagnostics use a single seed-42 checkpoint.
record.recipe_differences: Uses descriptor injection and CKA/RSA/cosine measurements in audio–MIDI encoders; it does not reproduce the original studies’ method or test scaling. This study is a research paper, not a repo.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment differs across descriptor/injection configurations; d4-a4r has the highest CKA while d4a4 has the highest seed-42 retrieval score. The paper reports both CKA and RSA, with increases over D0 for each augmented arm.

fits_no_version.finding: In jointly trained VICReg audio–MIDI encoders, injecting hand-crafted descriptors raises mean cross-encoder CKA from 0.435 (D0) to 0.659–0.794 and RSA from 0.446 to 0.646–0.761 (seed 42, 500 pairs). The highest-CKA arm (d4-a4r) is not the best at retrieval (79.8% vs 83.8% for d4a4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In contrastively co-trained cross-modal encoders, domain descriptors increase internal cross-encoder similarity, and greater internal alignment does not track retrieval performance monotonically.

fits_no_version.finding: Descriptor injection improves audio–MIDI retrieval S over D0, from 73.4% to 79.8–83.8% at seed 42 and from 75.2% to 80.7–84.0% as the five-seed mean.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On MAESTRO, descriptor injection improves bidirectional audio–MIDI retrieval over a descriptor-free VICReg baseline.

record.problems: The alignment diagnostics use a single seed-42 checkpoint and 500 matched pairs; only MAESTRO classical piano is tested. The paper notes that the audio encoder is partially initialized from pretrained weights. No model-size scaling or cross-seed representation comparison is reported, and CKA/RSA are not direct measurements of pairwise input-distance alignment.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results directly measure cross-modal representational alignment. Retrieval results are included as separate rows because the paper compares them with alignment; unrelated ablations, robustness tests, screening scores, probes, and visualization-only findings were left out.

untested.parts: No independently trained models and no model-size or capability sweep.
No independently trained vision/language (or any unimodal) models. Alignment is the training objective, and there is no scaling of capability.
Five seeds are reported only for retrieval, with no cross-seed representation comparison.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation test.
No feature or circuit universality analysis.
CKA and RSA are both reported but agree. Metric settings and OOD inputs are not varied for the alignment measure.
No test of plateau or of the causes of convergence across independent models.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T3 and its V2/V7 labels are rejected. The study's alignment is deliberately induced by its loss, and it compares descriptor arms of one jointly trained dual encoder, not independently trained models. The paper also notes that the audio encoder is partly initialised from pretrained weights. The parameter-matched control (Test 02: real 83.0% vs 73.6–75.0%) is a retrieval result and does not bear on any version.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability scaling sweep, nor comparison of independently trained models across architectures, objectives, data, or modalities.
Tests paired audio–MIDI encoders, not vision–language models; no scaling sweep of both modalities as they become more capable.
Five-seed results report retrieval performance, not shared features or subspaces across seeds.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired-data interchangeability test.
No test of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
Reports CKA and RSA alignment measures, but does not systematically test whether convergence depends on similarity-measure settings, neighbour count, or out-of-distribution inputs.
Reports incomplete alignment and a mismatch between alignment and retrieval, but does not test whether alignment plateaus or whether shared data/objectives cause it.

rows.subject: D0
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean CKA across 16 audio-by-MIDI transformer layer pairs on 500 matched pairs.
rows.note: CKA is a representation-similarity measure; it does not directly compare pairwise distances between inputs.
rows.check: D0 CKA is for encoders jointly trained to align (VICReg invariance loss), not independently trained models. It bears on no version, and 'partial' has no reference effect to compare against.

rows.subject: d4a4
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean CKA across 16 audio-by-MIDI transformer layer pairs on 500 matched pairs.
rows.note: The increase indicates greater measured alignment than D0, but CKA is not a direct pairwise-distance comparison.
rows.check: Measures the effect of descriptor injection on trained-in cross-encoder CKA (seed 42, one checkpoint). This is not convergence of independently trained models with capability.

rows.subject: a4r
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean CKA across 16 audio-by-MIDI transformer layer pairs on 500 matched pairs.
rows.note: The increase indicates greater measured alignment than D0, but CKA is not a direct pairwise-distance comparison.
rows.check: Same as r2: descriptor effect on alignment inside a jointly trained contrastive model.

rows.subject: d4-a4r
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean CKA across 16 audio-by-MIDI transformer layer pairs on 500 matched pairs.
rows.note: This arm has the highest reported CKA, but not the highest retrieval score.
rows.check: Same as r2. Highest CKA but not the best retrieval, which shows a dissociation rather than an alignment–capability link.

rows.subject: D0
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean RSA across the same cross-encoder layer-pair analysis.
rows.note: RSA is reported alongside CKA; the paper does not report a test of metric-setting sensitivity.
rows.check: RSA control for the jointly trained D0. It bears on no version.

rows.subject: d4a4
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean RSA across the same cross-encoder layer-pair analysis.
rows.note: RSA rises relative to D0, consistent with the CKA ordering for this arm.
rows.check: RSA rise from descriptor injection in a jointly trained system. It bears on no version.

rows.subject: D0
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarity for matched audio–MIDI embedding pairs.
rows.note: The paper gives this comparison explicitly for D0 and d4a4 only.
rows.check: Matched-pair cosine is essentially the quantity the training loss optimises, so it is not evidence of emergent convergence. It is reported only in the text, from visualisation (Sec. 5.8).

rows.subject: d4a4
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarity for matched audio–MIDI embedding pairs.
rows.note: The paper reports tighter matched-pair alignment for d4a4 than D0.
rows.check: Same as r9. Higher cosine for d4a4 (0.72 vs 0.58) reflects a better-optimised training objective.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Descriptor-augmented audio–MIDI arms compared with D0 on the seed-42 checkpoint
reader_labels.reason: CKA and RSA increase for all three augmented arms relative to D0, and the reported matched-pair cosine comparison increases for d4a4 (r2–r10).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Across descriptor configurations on the seed-42 checkpoint
reader_labels.reason: Alignment and retrieval are not monotonic: d4-a4r has higher CKA than d4a4 but lower retrieval S; this is a single audio–MIDI setting, not a scale test (r2–r4, r12–r14).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Alignment measures are below 1, and the arm with the highest CKA does not have the highest retrieval score; the results support partial rather than complete alignment tied directly to task performance (r1–r8, r12–r14).
